input: A defect-reduction project on a moulding cell cut the reject rate from 4.8% to 2.3% over one quarter. At 64k units per year, the change avoids about 1600 rejected units per year. The avoided count follows from the annual volume and the change in the reject rate: the rate difference, applied to the volume, gives the units no longer rejected. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. The shutdown shortened the running time inside the quarter, so both rates rest on a period that contains a planned stop rather than a full quarter of production. The comparison between the starting rate and the end rate is therefore a comparison across a period with a stop inside it, and the stop belongs to the record of the quarter rather than to a correction of the rates. The end rate is the figure that carries forward. Production planned at the annual volume and held at the end rate rejects fewer units in a year than production at the starting rate, and the avoided count states that difference on the annual volume. Read at another volume, the avoided count changes in proportion to the volume, while the rate change itself stays a property of the cell and of the quarter in which it was measured. The measure is a rate, so it does not depend on how many running hours the quarter happened to contain; the shutdown enters the result through the period over which the rates were measured, not through the definition of the measure itself. The result is a rate change on one cell over one quarter, with the shutdown inside the measurement period and named as part of the result.
